title: IPG Photonics Releases High-Power Lasers on new RI platform
body_text: MARLBOROUGH, Mass., June 20, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- IPG Photonics Corporation (NASDAQ: IPGP), the global leader in fiber laser technology, has released new high-power lasers built on a new rack-integrated platform. On display at Laser World of Photonics, June 24-27, 2025 in Munich, Germany, this product line delivers significant cost savings and operational advantages for manufacturers, including reduced floor space requirements, simplified integration, and enhanced reliability. IPG Unlocks Added Benefits for Manufacturers with Holistically Redesigned Laser Architecture These new RI lasers require 60% less floor space, reducing facility costs and enabling more flexible factory layouts. RI lasers take advantage of a new generation of IPG laser pump diodes with higher densities of power per volume, which in turn, lowers total cost of ownership. RI Platform Offers New Innovative Advantages for Manufacturing Beyond the reduction in size and weight, the new RI laser platform delivers more consistent processing results, reducing waste and setup time. The new platform provides simplified OEM integration and minimizes or eliminates laser damage or shutdown. Additionally, the RI architecture provides protection against condensation and can be cooled with water up to 25° C, resulting in the ability to increase the maximum operating temperature, while enabling even safer operation in humid environments. Further Improvements for Operational Efficiency and Customer Flexibility IPG continues to deliver on its promise of continuous innovation, as demonstrated by improving its line of already world-leading high-power lasers with unmatched specifications and new features. The RI platform offers higher flexibility and operational efficiency by allowing manufacturers to select optimized process parameters for multiple applications such as processing delicate materials that previously required separate equipment. Customers can discuss their specific applications and evaluate the technology in-person June 24-27, 2025 at Laser World of Photonics in Messe München in the IPG booth, Hall B3, Booth #218. About IPG Photonics Corporation IPG Photonics Corporation is the leader in high-power fiber lasers and amplifiers used primarily in materials processing and other diverse applications. The Company’s mission is to develop innovative laser solutions making the world a better place. IPG accomplishes this mission by delivering superior performance, reliability, and usability at a lower total cost of ownership compared with other types of lasers and non-laser tools, allowing end users to increase productivity and decrease costs. IPG is headquartered in Marlborough, Massachusetts and has more than 30 facilities worldwide. For more information, visit IPGPhotonics.com . Contact Eugene Fedotoff Senior Director, Investor Relations IPG Photonics Corporation 508-597-4713 efedotoff@IPGPhotonics.com

title: 6 Warning Signs Your Team May Be Vulnerable to Cyber Attacks – and Our Tips to Stay Safe
summary: Here are six signs your team may be vulnerable to cyber attacks, and some proven tips for managing your risk, including offering great awareness training.
body_text: Right now, scammers around the world are dreaming up new ways to get the better of you. And while you might know how to keep your networks, data, and money safe, cybersecurity is a team sport – you’ll still be at risk unless your colleagues do their part, too. So, how can you boost your team’s cybersecurity and stay safe together? You can start by looking at the biggest risk factors and making a plan to keep these under control. In this article, we look at six common signs your team may be vulnerable to cyber attacks. We’ll also offer some proven tips for addressing these vulnerabilities and managing your risk, including boosting your cybersecurity with unforgettable awareness training. Let’s start with something we’ve all become way too familiar with lately. #1: Your team is working remotely Over recent years, millions of people have shifted into working remotely at least part of the time, including an estimated 60% of knowledge workers . And while this flexibility has been a welcome change for some, it creates a whole new set of cybersecurity risks. That’s because working across a range of WiFi networks (especially public networks) increases the attack surface scammers can use to access company systems. A distributed workforce also makes it a lot harder for your IT team to maintain core network protections, and creates the risk that unauthorized people might be accessing sensitive data. Given these risks, it’s unsurprising that we’ve seen an estimated 238% increase in cyber attacks coinciding with the shift to remote work over the last few years. How to help your distributed workforce stay secure A distributed workforce presents security challenges, but you can keep your team safe by: Encouraging people to use a VPN or secure WiFi network, and to avoid risky public networks (for example, WiFi in airports, libraries, or cafes). Teaching people how to identify and report cyber attack attempts targeting remote workers (for example, invoice fraud impersonating managers or accounting teams). Mandating the latest antivirus and Data Loss Prevention (DLP) software – and making it easy to report spam emails and attempted data exfiltration. And speaking of distributed workforces, here’s another common cybersecurity vulnerability. Learn more: 3 Ways to Take Control of Your Digital Footprint and Stop Giving Scammers a Head Start #2: People are using their own devices for work With the shift to cloud-based systems, the days of working on a single company-owned device are well and truly over. Now, 97% of executives access work accounts on personal devices, with many of us mixing work and personal use across different phones, laptops, and tablets. This might be faster and more convenient, but it turns every device into a potential entry point for scammers. And unsurprisingly, scammers have capitalized on this shift, with attacks on mobile devices growing by 50% over recent years – including attempts to access company networks. How to turn BYOD into NBD If your team works across a mix of personal and company devices, you can encourage them to: Keep their operating systems updated, as having out-of-date operating systems increases the risk your team’s devices could be exploited. Be extremely cautious about downloading apps, making sure they’re not disguising malware. Limit the people with access to their devices, for example, family members and children. Set strong passwords and access codes, including using a password manager. Follow company guidelines on what happens if a device with work access is lost or stolen. #3: You’re relying on generic cybersecurity awareness training A cybersecurity awareness training program is the single most effective step you can take to keep your team safe against potential attacks. This training helps people identify the most common and disruptive scams, and teaches them the techniques they need to stay secure. But to get this right, you need cybersecurity training tailored to individual needs and work contexts. Unfortunately, a lot of the training organizations provide is still generic and forgettable. How to provide the awareness training people deserve People are used to boring cybersecurity training that feels just like any other annual compliance exercise. That’s why they switch off, and why scammers win so often. Instead, we need to: Invest in tailored awareness training to match individual needs and experience levels. Offer people fun and engaging training experiences based on real stories. Let people learn where they already work, for example, in Slack or Teams. Cover foundational topics like password best practices and data security alongside advanced subjects like spear phishing, digital footprints, and AI-powered deep fakes. Follow up training with phishing simulations to test people on how much they remember. At Riot, we make it easy to boost your cybersecurity awareness through tailored training people can’t help but love. Chat to one of our experts to find out more . #4: You aren’t encrypting or backing up your data In 2019, two Facebook app developers accidentally leaked unencrypted records relating to over 540 million users , including names, photos, location check-ins, and passwords. While this wasn’t malicious, it illustrates the risks involved with failing to encrypt and back up data adequately. Unprotected data storage and administration is a big sign you and your team might be vulnerable to cyber attacks. Specifically, if you’re failing to encrypt sensitive data, this opens you to the risk of catastrophic breaches should fraudsters access your systems and demand ransom. How to take the stress out of data management Data management might sound technical, but it doesn’t have to be. You need to: Encrypt and protect sensitive data everywhere, and keep keys secure – particularly when sharing data with third-party business partners. Make a multi-pronged backup and recovery strategy to spread the risk of data loss. Invest in a tool to notify you whenever any company logins are affected by data breaches. #5: Your network isn’t adequately segmented Another technical vulnerability relates to network segmentation and user access monitoring. Specifically, users accessing wider parts of your organization’s network with the same login creates a higher risk of cyber attack – and so does failing to actively monitor user access. For example, take the Banner Health data breach . In 2016, fraudsters managed to access the company’s databases through its food and beverage payment systems, eventually accessing sensitive health information relating to 2.81 million patients. A subsequent investigation found the health provider hadn’t adequately assessed the risk of cyber attacks targeting its single shared network, and hadn’t been actively monitoring user access to identify potential attacks. How to set access to minimize your risks You can address the risks involved with unsegmented network access by: Separating the most valuable company assets in separate networks and limiting user access. Developing a company-wide policy governing who has access to which parts of the network. Adopting the principle of least privilege when it comes to data access. Limiting third-party network access – including supply chain partners (see below). #6: Your supply chain partners are vulnerable to cyber attacks Finally, a word on your supply chain partners. Scammers are now regularly targeting organizations through attacks on their supply chain partners – particularly when these partners have access to sensitive data. That’s why it’s so crucial to ensure a shared commitment to cybersecurity across your business network – especially your supply chain partners. For an example of how this can go wrong, let’s look at Okta. In 2021, the company experienced a major data breach as a result of security vulnerabilities on behalf of Sykes, one of its customer support providers. This shows why active third-party cybersecurity management is so crucial. How to keep your whole network safe You can proactively address the risks involved with third-party cybersecurity practices by: Requiring supply chain partners to comply with core cybersecurity and data protection measures. Restricting third-party access to systems and data, and actively monitoring access. For EU organizations, observing NIS2 requirements to investigate supply chain partner cybersecurity protections and take reasonable steps to address any vulnerabilities. Ready to make NIS2 a walk in the park? Download our free six-step compliance checklist . A checklist to make NIS2 compliance simple and easy. Fight cybersecurity vulnerabilities with great awareness training When it comes to stopping cyber attacks, it isn’t enough for you to roll solo – your whole team needs to know how to stay secure. Unfortunately, 85% of all successful data breaches involve human error, meaning your colleagues could end up being the reason you get scammed. That’s why impactful awareness training can make such a big difference in proactively managing the threat of cyber attacks. With Riot, your whole team can learn about the latest scams, including AI-powered deep fakes, phishing, and much more. This way, they know exactly what to do to reduce the risk of cyber attacks, and what to do in case of real-life scam attempts. Even better, you can test your team with our simple and intuitive phishing simulation platform, crafting the kinds of attacks people are mostly likely to face and teaching them how to stay safe. To find out how Riot can help you and your team stay on top of the latest cyber threats, get in touch with one of our experts today . title: How to Create a Resume That Passes ATS | Step-by-Step Guide
summary: Learn how to create an ATS-friendly resume that increases your chances of landing an interview. Follow step-by-step tips on formatting, keyword optimization, and best resume-building practices.
body_text: In today’s competitive job market, many companies use Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) to filter resumes before they reach recruiters. If your resume is not ATS-friendly, it might get rejected automatically—no matter how qualified you are. This guide will teach you how to create a resume that passes ATS checks , ensuring your application reaches hiring managers and boosts your chances of landing an interview. Step 1: Understand How ATS Works Before creating your resume, it’s crucial to understand how an Applicant Tracking System (ATS) works. ATS scans resumes for specific keywords, formatting, and structure to determine if they match the job description. Key Features of ATS - Keyword Matching – ATS looks for relevant keywords from the job description. - Proper Formatting – Avoid fancy fonts, graphics, and tables that ATS may not read. - Clear Section Headings – Use standard headings like "Education," "Work Experience," and "Skills." - File Format Matters – Submit your resume in PDF or DOCX format to ensure ATS compatibility. An easy way to create an ATS-friendly resume is by using Kaagaz Resume Maker , which ensures correct formatting and keyword optimization. For more resume tips, read 5 Resume Mistakes to Avoid . Step 2: Choose the Right Resume Format Selecting the correct resume format plays a significant role in passing ATS filters . The best format for ATS is: ATS-Approved Resume Formats - Reverse Chronological – Lists work experience from most recent to oldest. - Hybrid (Combination) – Combines skills and experience for a well-rounded profile. Avoid creative resume formats with columns, images, and infographics, as ATS might not read them properly. Best Practice: Use a simple, professional template available on Kaagaz Resume Maker . Step 3: Optimize Your Resume with Keywords Many resumes get rejected because they lack job-specific keywords that ATS looks for. How to Find the Right Keywords? -Copy the job description and identify frequently used skills and industry terms . -Use an ATS Resume Checker to test keyword optimization. -Include both abbreviations and full terms (e.g., “SEO” and “Search Engine Optimization”). Example: If applying for a marketing role, include keywords like "SEO," "Google Ads," "content marketing," and "social media management." Best Practice: Use Kaagaz Resume Maker to ensure your resume is keyword-optimized for ATS . Step 4: Structure Your Resume for ATS Compatibility A well-structured resume increases your chances of passing ATS screening. Follow this standard structure: Essential Resume Sections - Professional Summary – A brief overview of your qualifications. - Work Experience – List jobs in reverse chronological order. - Education – Include degree, institution, and graduation year. - Skills Section – Highlight relevant hard and soft skills. - Certifications & Achievements – Showcase additional qualifications. Pro Tip: Use simple fonts (Arial, Calibri, Times New Roman, size 11-12) and bullet points for easy readability. Are you a fresher looking for a job? Mistakes to Avoid - Using tables, images, or columns – ATS may not read these correctly. - Not customizing your resume – One-size-fits-all resumes fail ATS checks. - Using uncommon fonts or colors – Stick to professional black-and-white formatting. - Incorrect file format – Always submit PDF or DOCX format. title: EOR Compliance in the US: Everything Employers Need to Know
summary: In this guide, we’ll walk through what “EOR compliance” means in the U.S., key legal pitfalls, best practices, and how HireArt can help ensure you stay on the right side of the law.
body_text: When expanding your workforce across U.S. states or hiring remote employees in different jurisdictions, one of the most critical challenges is EOR compliance. In this guide, we’ll walk through what “EOR compliance” means in the U.S., key legal pitfalls, best practices, and how HireArt can help ensure you stay on the right side of the law. What Is EOR Compliance? “EOR compliance” refers to the legal, regulatory, and administrative obligations that must be met by an Employer of Record (EOR) and its client when employees are engaged under that arrangement. An EOR is a third-party entity that becomes the legal employer of workers on behalf of another company, handling payroll, taxes, benefits, and compliance with labor laws, while the client retains day-to-day control of work, projects, and performance. In the U.S., EOR compliance covers both federal and state regulations, which can vary widely by jurisdiction. Some of the core compliance domains include: Employment eligibility and I-9 / E-Verify Wage and hour laws (minimum wage, overtime, predictive scheduling) Payroll tax withholding, reporting, and unemployment insurance Workers’ compensation Employee benefits and leave (e.g. FMLA, state family leave laws) Worker classification (employee vs. independent contractor) Notice, wage statements, and record keeping Terminations, severance, and final pay Local laws and ordinances (city or county mandates) An EOR is expected to assume many of these responsibilities on behalf of the hiring company, but clarity regarding responsibility allocation is crucial. ‍ Why EOR Compliance Matters in the US 1. Complexity across states. U.S. federal laws set minimum standards, but states and even localities can impose stricter requirements. For example, states may mandate additional leave, unique pay frequency rules, or overtime thresholds more generous than the federal standard. 2. Worker misclassification risk. Misclassifying a worker as an independent contractor instead of an employee can lead to back taxes, penalties, and lawsuits. An EOR should help guide proper classification. 3. Liability and risk mitigation. If an EOR is truly acting as the legal employer, it can protect the client from certain compliance risks, shifting the burden of regulatory responsibility. 4. Scalability and speed. When entering new states or hiring in places where your company doesn’t already have a legal entity, leveraging an EOR with compliance infrastructure helps you scale faster while mitigating legal risk. ‍ Key U.S. Compliance Areas in Depth Employment Eligibility & I-9/E-Verify Under federal law, all U.S. employees must complete Form I-9 to verify identity and eligibility to work. Some employers (e.g. federal contractors) or states may also require use of E-Verify. An EOR must maintain properly completed I-9 records and comply with audit requests. Wage & Hour Laws The Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) is the baseline, but many states have higher minimum wages or stricter overtime triggers. EORs must ensure that pay, overtime, record keeping, and break/rest rules comply with applicable state law. Payroll Taxes & Reporting An EOR must withhold and remit federal income tax, Social Security, Medicare, and relevant state and local taxes. It must file quarterly and annual returns (e.g. Form 941, Form W-2s) and handle unemployment insurance contributions. Workers’ Compensation & Unemployment Insurance Each state has unique workers’ compensation and unemployment insurance systems. The EOR must register appropriately, pay premiums, and manage claims in compliance with state regulations. Benefits, Leave & Protections Federal laws like FMLA and ADA apply, and states may have additional leave laws (e.g. paid sick leave, paid family leave). EORs must integrate these into benefits administration and ensure employee rights are honored. Termination & Final Pay EOR compliance also extends to lawful termination, final pay deadlines, severance (where required), and any mandated notices (e.g. WARN Act). Some states demand immediate payment of all wages owed at termination. ‍ Shared Responsibilities: What the Client vs. the EOR Must Handle Even with an EOR, not all compliance tasks can or should be handed off. Clear delineation matters. ‍ Responsibility EOR’s Role Client’s Role / Oversight Legal employment status & contract Draft and maintain compliant contracts Approve contract terms Payroll, taxes, withholding Run payroll, remit taxes, file reports Fund payroll, provide compensation data Benefits, insurance, leaves Administer benefits, leave compliance Determine benefit strategy Worker classification guidance Advise on classification Provide job duties, control I-9 / employment eligibility Maintain I-9, E-Verify if applicable Provide onboarding data Performance management, daily work No Full responsibility Termination compliance Execute termination in line with the law Initiate termination, inform EOR ‍ Common Compliance Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them Ignoring state-specific laws — assuming federal law suffices. Misclassifying workers — e.g. labeling someone “contractor” when control, hours, or expectations align with employee status. Overlooking city-level ordinances — cities like San Francisco, Seattle, or New York may impose local mandates. Delays or errors in payroll/tax filing — missing deadlines risks penalties. Inadequate I-9 / E-Verify record maintenance — audits of I-9 files can be triggered by ICE. Failing to incorporate new leave laws — e.g. state paid family leave programs. Ambiguous agreement scopes — poor delineation can lead to liability disputes between company and EOR. Best practices include: regular audits of compliance protocols, updating contracts when laws change, employing legal counsel in key states, and choosing an EOR with strong compliance track record. ‍ Compliance to Improve Employee Experience t HireArt, we believe compliance isn’t just about risk mitigation—it’s about trust. A compliant, W-2 employment experience helps workers feel valued, supported, and secure. When compliance works well, it actually improves worker satisfaction, retention, and performance. Here’s how: 1. W-2 Status Means Greater Stability and Benefits Unlike 1099 arrangements, W-2 employment ensures workers receive steady paychecks, tax withholdings handled on their behalf, and eligibility for benefits such as health insurance, PTO, and retirement plans. This creates real security for professionals working on long-term projects—a theme we’ve discussed in our article “Why Compliance Is the Foundation of a Better Contractor Experience.” 2. Transparent Pay and Protections Build Trust From overtime pay to paid sick leave, compliant employment ensures workers are fairly compensated and protected under law. Creating predictable processes and consistent policies make workers feel safe and respected. This is the secret key to building engagement across contingent teams. 3. Legal Protections Promote Equity Compliance brings parity between contract and full-time workers. It eliminates gray areas that often lead to unequal treatment in pay or opportunity. By using an EOR like HireArt that adheres to strict wage-and-hour and anti-discrimination standards, companies demonstrate their commitment to fairness and inclusion. 4. Consistency Across States Enhances Experience A consistent employment experience—regardless of where workers are based—helps teams feel unified. 5. Compliance as a Cultural Advantage Finally, compliance can actually elevate your brand. Workers talk, and reputation spreads. When contractors know they’ll be paid accurately, receive clear documentation, and access the benefits they deserve, your company becomes an employer of choice—especially in the competitive AI, tech, and professional contracting markets HireArt serves. ‍ How HireArt Can Help You Ensure EOR Compliance At HireArt, we understand that compliance is foundational for any scalable workforce solution. Our approach to EOR compliance includes: Expertise in multi-state employment law — we stay current with federal, state, and local regulations. Clear role delineation — we define who is responsible for each compliance item in the engagement. Seamless payroll & tax handling — ensuring accurate tax withholding, quarterly filings, unemployment, and workers’ compensation. Contract drafting and maintenance — we craft employment agreements that comply across jurisdictions. Ongoing monitoring & audits — we periodically review compliance mechanisms to catch gaps or changes in law. Termination support & compliance — we guide and execute lawful termination procedures. EOR compliance in the U.S. is complex — and noncompliance can be costly in fines, reputational damage, or litigation. With HireArt as your EOR partner, you can expand or maintain a distributed U.S. workforce with confidence, knowing your compliance obligations are managed.

title: How to rank higher on Airbnb: a host’s guide to getting seen
summary: Tired of being buried in Airbnb search? We break down the algorithm into three core pillars to help you send the right signals and get seen.
body_text: How to rank higher on Airbnb: a host’s guide to getting seen by Guesty Marketing Team | July 29, 2026 Reading time: 8 minutes Share Guesty Marketing Team Share If your listing is buried on page five of Airbnb’s search results, it might as well not exist. You have a great property, but visibility is everything. The algorithm is a system designed to reward hosts who provide the best possible guest experience. Treat it like a scorecard. Think of the algorithm as Airbnb’s matchmaker. Its only goal is to connect the right guest with the right stay, every time. It tracks dozens of signals to figure out which listings are most likely to result in a happy guest and a five-star review. To climb the rankings, you need to send the right signals. Your entire strategy can be broken down into three core pillars: delivering an unforgettable guest experience , being a relentlessly reliable host, and creating a listing that converts lookers into bookers. TL;DR The Airbnb algorithm rewards hosts who deliver great guest experiences, prove their reliability, and create appealing listings. Consistent five-star reviews are the single most powerful signal of quality you can send. Your response time, calendar accuracy, and cancellation rate directly impact your search placement. Listings with professional photos, compelling descriptions, and in-demand amenities get more clicks and bookings, which boosts their rank. Enable Instant Book. It’s a massive ranking factor and reduces friction for guests. Set competitive prices that adjust to demand. Stale pricing signals a stale listing. A vacation rental software like Guesty® automates the tedious tasks that fuel your ranking, from calendar syncs to guest messaging. Pillar 1: Deliver an unforgettable guest experience The algorithm’s top priority is guest satisfaction. Every positive review is a vote of confidence that tells Airbnb your listing is a safe bet. This is the most important pillar. Get this right, and the algorithm will work for you. Aim for consistent 5-star reviews High ratings are the fuel for your ranking engine. Airbnb’s algorithm prioritizes listings that consistently delight guests. Every four-star review for “Cleanliness” or “Accuracy” is a drag on your visibility. Your goal is to create a system for earning great reviews. This means setting accurate expectations with your listing, communicating proactively before and during the stay, and ensuring your property is impeccably clean and well-stocked. A small, thoughtful touch, like a list of local coffee shops or a few bottles of water in the fridge, can be the difference between a four-star and a five-star stay. Work towards Superhost status The Superhost badge is a clear signal to guests and the algorithm that you are a top-tier host. Airbnb’s criteria for becoming a Superhost provide a roadmap for climbing the rankings. You need to maintain a 4.8+ overall rating, keep a cancellation rate below 1%, achieve a 90%+ response rate, and complete at least 10 stays (or 100 nights over three stays). Focus on meeting these four criteria. Even if you don’t get the badge this quarter, aiming for these metrics will force you to adopt the habits of a top-ranking host. Pillar 2: Be a reliable and responsive host Airbnb wants to send its users to hosts who are active, engaged, and dependable. Every interaction you have on the platform before a booking is a signal of your reliability. Lagging on these metrics tells the algorithm you might not provide a smooth experience. Respond to inquiries instantly Your response rate is a direct measure of your attentiveness. Airbnb tracks how quickly you reply to new messages and prioritizes hosts who respond fastest. A guest asks about parking at 10 PM. Another sends a booking inquiry at 6 AM. Juggling these messages is how response times slip below the crucial 90% threshold. Centralize every conversation into a Unified Inbox to respond in minutes, not hours. For even faster replies, Guesty’s AI agents, like ReplyAI , can handle common questions instantly based on your rules, ensuring you maintain a near-perfect response rate around the clock. Keep your calendar updated daily An accurate calendar is a sign of an active, professional host. The algorithm favors listings that are frequently updated. If you also list your property on other platforms like Booking.com, Vrbo, or Expedia, manually blocking off dates is a direct path to a double booking. A double booking leads to a cancellation, which is one of the biggest penalties to your ranking. Use a Channel Manager to sync your availability across every booking site automatically. A reservation on Vrbo should instantly block the dates on Airbnb without you lifting a finger. Avoid cancellations at all costs Boost your short term rentals today Get started Host-initiated cancellations are a massive red flag to the algorithm. A cancellation creates a terrible experience for a guest and damages trust in the platform. Airbnb penalizes hosts for this severely with fees and a drop in search ranking. Obviously, emergencies happen. But cancellations for preventable reasons, like a double booking or a pricing mistake, are devastating to your visibility. Double-check your availability and pricing rules to ensure you never have to cancel on a guest. Enable Instant Book for higher visibility Guests love convenience. Instant Book removes the friction of waiting for a host to approve a request. Because it improves the user experience, Airbnb gives a significant ranking boost to listings that have it enabled. It also adds your listing to a search filter that many guests use, immediately increasing your exposure. If you’re worried about unsuitable guests, you can set booking requirements, such as only accepting guests who have a government-issued ID on file or positive reviews from other hosts. Pillar 3: Create a high-converting listing Your listing is your digital storefront. A beautiful, informative, and compelling listing gets more clicks, a higher “add to wishlist” rate, and more bookings. The algorithm tracks this engagement as a sign of your listing’s appeal and rewards you with better placement. Write compelling titles and descriptions Your title is your headline.
